name: Game, Flip, Flop
description: Game, Flip, Flop is a high-stakes variation of the American Rummy game 'Tunk' (or Tonk). Originating in Dayton, Ohio, it is famous for its three distinct betting pots: 'Game', 'Flip', and 'Flop'. While the core gameplay follows standard Rummy melding rules, the 'Flip' and 'Flop' pots introduce a side-betting element based entirely on having the lowest cards of specific suits dealt in your initial hand. It is a fast-paced gambling game where players can win pots without even playing a card.

history.origins: The game was documented by Chad Shumate as a local specialty of Dayton, Ohio. Its roots lie in the African-American card tradition of 'Tunk' (Tonk), which was widely played by soldiers and jazz musicians in the mid-20th century.
timeline: 1940s: Tonk becomes popular in the US.
Late 20th Century: 'Game, Flip, Flop' evolves in Dayton as a more aggressive variant with side-pots.
Present: Remains a regional favorite in Ohio home games.
history.cultural: Often played for money, with strictly enforced rules about 'paying for the pots' before each deal.
history.evolution: It added the 'Flip' and 'Flop' mechanics to standard Tonk, shifting the focus from pure hand management to initial deal luck.

setup.dealing: Deal 5 cards to each player. turn the next card (Dealer's last card) FACE-UP. This is the FLIP CARD.

rules.objective: Win the 'Game' pot by having the lowest points or going out, and win the 'Flip/Flop' pots by holding low cards.
rules.gameplay:
1. Players reveal cards to claim Flip/Flop pots immediately.
2. Standard Draw/Discard Rummy play ensues.
3. Melds: Sets (3+ of a kind) or Runs (3+ sequential in suit).
4. Dropping: At the start of your turn, you can place your cards face-up to 'Drop' (Knock). If you have the lowest point total, you win the Game Pot. If someone has lower/equal, you lose double ('Caught').
keyRules: Pay to Play: You can't win a pot you didn't contribute to.

strategy.basic: Check for 49/50 immediately. A starting hand of five face cards/10s is rare but instantly ends the game.
strategy.intermediate: The Drop Threshold: Since face cards are 10, hand totals are high. If you have under 15 points early in the game, it is usually safe to 'Drop' and take the pot.
strategy.advanced: Defensive Tunk: If you see a player has won the Flip and Flop stakes, they are 'freerolling' the Game pot. Play aggressively to Tunk out or Drop early to prevent them from sweeping the table and taking all three pots.
tips: Always keep a 'reserve' stake. Losing a 'Caught' drop costs double.
Don't hold onto high cards hoping for a run. In Game, Flip, Flop, points are liabilities.

scoring.description: Three-pot betting system: game pot, flip pot, and flop pot with claims based on the original dealt cards.
scoring.winCondition: Flip pot goes to lowest card in flip suit; flop pot goes to lowest card in the other suit of same color if present. Game pot is won by valid drop, tunk out, or lowest hand when stock ends; double-game-pot outcomes apply for 50, tunk out, and caught drops.

synthesis.shortDescription: A high-stakes Ohio variant of Tonk/Rummy with three separate betting pots (Game, Flip, Flop) where side-pot bonuses are determined by initial deal luck.
